content:
Sam (SRE): heads up — multiple customer escalations for 502/504 from hosted inference in east-us2. Spike started ~15:34 UTC and is still ongoing. dashboards: gateway 502 rate ~6-8%

incident-bot: ALERT: hosted-api-gateway.eastus2 502-rate > 5% (15:36 UTC)

Jordan (Support): Customer 'BrightPay' opened a P1 at 15:35. They included curl repro: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -d '{"model":"rw-v1-large","input":"hello"}'
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Server: redwood-gateway
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"upstream_unreachable"}
```
They see intermittent 502s, every 10-30s. Happening across multiple customers in the east-us2 region.

Anya (NetOps): I'm seeing packet loss and spikes on inter-az paths (az-a <-> az-b). BGP shows rapid peer flaps to ASN 64521 (transit). Summary from our edge: 
```
15:33:21 RIB: BGP neighbor 198.51.100.4 went DOWN, reason=Transport reset
15:34:05 IFACE: eth3 tx drops=620 rx drops=0
15:34:06 netstat -s | grep -i retrans: tcpRetrans=459
```
Kei (Runtime): Runtime logs from the gateway show repeated upstream connection resets when trying to reach model-pool east-us2-az-b: 
```
[15:34:12] gateway: upstream_connect error: connection reset by peer (while proxying to 10.10.42.7:443)
[15:34:47] gateway: upstream_timeout after 5s
```
We have sticky routing to AZ-b for some model shards; that would explain 502s when that AZ path degrades.

CarrierNOC: we've been alerted by our transit partner — microbursting on PE-core link to region-east-us2 causing intermittent egress drops. Investigating buffering and queue scheduling. Peering session itself is flapping due to hardware backpressure.

Sam (SRE): can we get a quick mitigation: 1) fail traffic from AZ-b -> AZ-a where possible, 2) disable sticky shard routing for affected models to spread to healthy AZs, 3) throttle large concurrent clients to reduce pressure.

Kei (Runtime): doing step 2 now — flipping shard affinity off for model family rw-v1 for east-us2; applying service intent to prefer az-a and az-c. Patching routing config: 
```
# runtime intent change
route.override(eastus2) = { prefer_az: ["az-a","az-c"], sticky_affinity: false }
```
Patch applied at 15:50 UTC.

Anya (NetOps): opened ticket with transit ASN 64521 (ref 78921). Requested immediate buffer tuning and to check for faulty port on PE2. Also moving some spine-egress paths to alternate peer for east-us2.

Jordan (Support): Posting interim note to BrightPay: "we're seeing a regional network issue impacting east-us2 with partial packet loss; engineering is rerouting traffic and we'll update in 30m." They asked for ETA — I said TBD but will follow up after rollback/mitigation.

Sam (SRE): I'm running tcpdump on the gateway egress toward AZ-b to capture resets. grabbing 30s pcap now: 
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth3 host 10.10.42.7 and port 443 -w /tmp/eastus2-azb.pcap -c 5000
```
Noting a pattern of bursts where a bunch of retransmits then a reset. I'll upload to incident bucket.

CarrierNOC: We effected an egress buffer tuning for PE2 and removed a suspected faulty SFP at 16:08 UTC. After that, we saw a drop in device-level tx drops. Looks like immediate hardware/queueing problem.

Kei (Runtime): after routing change, gateway 502 rate dropped to ~1.2% by 16:15 UTC. Rolling rollback of sticky affinity will stay for 45m to confirm.

Jordan (Support): BrightPay confirms reduced errors at 16:18 UTC. They still saw a couple of timeouts but much better.

Sam (SRE): actions summary: 
- NetOps ticket with carrier (64521) ref 78921 (Anya)
- Runtime disabled sticky shard affinity (Kei)
- SRE collected pcap and logs and uploaded to s3://incidents/2102345678/ (Sam)
- Support sent customer update (Jordan)
- Carrier replaced SFP + buffer tune (CarrierNOC)

CarrierNOC: final note — we're continuing to monitor for residual microbursts; recommended to keep traffic spread across azs for 2 hours.

Sam (SRE): we'll keep this thread open until metrics stable for 1h and carrier confirms. Tentative resolve window 17:20 UTC. Marking follow-ups: postmortem to include why shard affinity was sticky for those models and consider autoswitch on inter-az packet loss > 1%.

Kei (Runtime): adding a short-term guard: if inter-az RTT > 30ms or packet-loss > 1% for 60s, automatically prefer alternate az. Patch PR #4321 queued.

incident-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: hosted-api-gateway.eastus2 502-rate returned to baseline at 16:22 UTC

Sam (SRE): confirmed metrics stable; closing now. Will create postmortem template and assign owners.

Jordan (Support): closing customer cases with summary & apology.

-- end of thread --
